classification.difficultyReason: Derive individual normal-curve region percentages from the three supplied central percentages using symmetry and subtraction.

content.prompt:
Using only the given information, fill in the missing percentages of the normal curve.

(You will need to do this in an exam as the normal curve is not given to you.)

spec.description: Unfilled normal curve with seven labelled ticks, dashed vertical guides and three aligned central-interval arrows. Decorative orange and green source strokes use house black; solid curve and dashed guides retain their distinct roles.
spec.mathematics: The central intervals from -1 to 1, -2 to 2 and -3 to 3 contain approximately 68%, 95% and 99.7%, respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three supplied central percentages are visible. Individual region percentages are left for student annotation.

answer.short: From left to right, the eight regions contain approximately $0.15\%,\ 2.35\%,\ 13.5\%,\ 34\%,\ 34\%,\ 13.5\%,\ 2.35\%,\ 0.15\%$.
answer.worked:
By symmetry, matching regions on either side of $z=0$ have equal percentages.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Between }0\text{ and }1&=\frac{68\%}{2}\\&=34\%\\\text{Between }1\text{ and }2&=\frac{95\%-68\%}{2}\\&=13.5\%\\\text{Between }2\text{ and }3&=\frac{99.7\%-95\%}{2}\\&=2.35\%\\\text{Beyond }3&=\frac{100\%-99.7\%}{2}\\&=0.15\%\end{align*}$$

Reflect these percentages across $z=0$ to complete the left half. These are empirical-rule approximations.

spec.description: Complete self-contained answer figure with all eight region percentages. Leader arrows identify narrow outer regions without crowding their labels.
